candidates.title: eDKM: An Efficient and Accurate Train-Time Weight Clustering for Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Since Large Language Models or LLMs have demonstrated high-quality performance on many complex language tasks, there is a great interest in bringing these LLMs to mobile devices for faster responses and better privacy protection. However, the size of LLMs (i.e., billions of parameters) requires highly effective compression to fit into storage-limited devices. Among many compression techniques, weight-clustering, a form of non-linear quantization, is one of the leading candidates for LLM compression, and supported by modern smartphones. Yet, its training overhead is prohibitively significant for LLM fine-tuning. Especially, Differentiable KMeans Clustering, or DKM, has shown the state-of-the-art trade-off between compression ratio and accuracy regression, but its large memory complexity makes it nearly impossible to apply to train-time LLM compression. In this letter, we propose a memory-efficient DKM implementation, eDKM powered by novel techniques to reduce the memory footprint of DKM by orders of magnitudes. For a given tensor to be saved on CPU for the backward pass of DKM, we compressed the tensor by applying uniquification and sharding after checking if there is no duplicated tensor previously copied to CPU. Our experimental results demonstrate that eDKM can fine-tune and compress a pretrained LLaMA 7B model from 12.6 GB to 2.5 GB (3 b/weight) with the Alpaca dataset by reducing the train-time memory footprint of a decoder layer by 130×, while delivering good accuracy on broader LLM benchmarks (i.e., 77.7% for PIQA, 66.1% for Winograde, and so on).
candidates.reason: LLMをモバイル機器へ載せるための重みクラスタリング（非線形量子化）DKMについて、後方計算用テンソルのCPU保存方法を工夫してメモリ量を桁違いに削減したeDKMを提案しており、推論向け圧縮手法そのものへの直接の技術的貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: SpecCTMC: Exact Speculative Simulation of Diffusion Language Model Continuous-Time Markov Chains
candidates.abstract: Masked diffusion language models offer parallel text generation, but independently sampling multiple tokens can disrupt their dependencies and change the output distribution. Exact continuous-time sampling avoids this approximation, yet typically requires one sequential model evaluation per token. We introduce SpecCTMC, a training-free speculative sampler that reduces this sequential bottleneck without a separate draft model. SpecCTMC proposes successive token updates using previously computed model predictions, evaluates their intermediate states in parallel, and applies an exact acceptance-and-correction procedure. We prove that SpecCTMC preserves the joint distribution of event times, generation order, and token values of the underlying continuous-time Markov chain. It therefore introduces neither time-discretization error nor additional factorization error from parallel decoding. Experiments on LLaDA-8B-Instruct and Dream-v0-Instruct-7B across five benchmarks demonstrate 1.73-4.38x fewer sequential model evaluations than direct continuous-time sampling, while preserving the reference sampling distribution. Our code is available at: https://github.com/kasakh/specctmc
candidates.reason: マスク拡散言語モデルの逐次サンプリングに対し、過去の予測で後続トークン更新を提案し並列評価と厳密な受容・修正を行うSpecCTMCを提案し、逐次モデル評価回数を1.73〜4.38倍削減したと示す投機的デコードへの直接の貢献である。

candidates.title: Improving Iteration-based Non-Autoregressive Language Model With Time Step Awareness
candidates.venue: International Conference on Parallel and Distributed Systems
candidates.abstract: Iteration-based non-autoregressive (INAR) language models make a trade-off between quality and latency by controlling the number of decoding iterations. Recently proposed diffusion language models, which explicitly model the diffusion process by splitting the intractable probability distribution into simpler distribution along the dimension of the time step, achieve comparable generation quality against the autoregressive (AR) model. However, diffusion models need many iterations to get the same generation quality as AR, which leads to slower generation speed. To reach higher performance with fewer steps, we propose a Conditional Masked Language Model with Time step Awareness (CMLMTA) that combines a discrete forward diffusion process with Conditional Masked Language Model (CMLM), one of leading INAR model. Explicit modeling time steps also allows us to employ curriculum learning strategy along the dimension of time step to make further improvement. Experiments on multiple machine translation tasks show that our model outperforms other diffusion models and CMLM by 1-3 BLEU.
candidates.reason: 反復型非自己回帰・拡散言語モデルについて時間ステップ認識を組み込んだCMLMTAを提案し、より少ないデコード反復で機械翻訳のBLEUを1〜3点改善すると示しており、生成デコードの反復回数と品質のトレードオフへの直接の技術的貢献である。
